title: interop-fallback-policy-for-tool-calls-with-naming-mapper-and-telemetry
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: Customers and internal infra observe a class of failures when LLM-generated tool invocations reference legacy function identifiers or colloquial tool names. These failures are amplified in streaming responses where a mid-stream fallback to an alternative tool can produce inconsistent structured outputs and break downstream consumers.

Goal: Implement a deterministic interop fallback policy that: (1) resolves tool identifiers across OpenAI-style tools and legacy functions using a mapper that preserves provenance and idempotency tokens, (2) chooses fallback candidates using semantic + lexical scoring with configurable policy weights, (3) supports in-flight streaming fallbacks with an API contract that guarantees structured-output fidelity or graceful degradation, and (4) emits telemetry to diagnose mismatch patterns and drive alias backfills.

Scope: runtime routing layer, name-mapper table, a small shim in the streaming dispatcher to perform safe mid-stream substitution, server-side telemetry events and a migration/rollout plan. This ticket coordinates the runtime implementation and rollout. It does NOT include a UI for editing aliases (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Name-mapper accepts mappings of the form {canonical_id, aliases[], description_hash} and preserves original invocation provenance in logs
Fallback decision is deterministic given same inputs and policy weights (documented in design doc)

When a fallback occurs mid-stream, the dispatcher emits a structured 'fallback-event' chunk and either continues the selected tool's output or completes with a documented degradation token — no corrupted JSON in structured outputs
Telemetry events emitted for every unresolved alias, chosen fallback, and confidence score (fields: alias, canonical_id, score, method, request_id)
Integration tests covering: exact-match, alias-match (lexical), semantic-match (embedding+threshold), and 'no-match' behaviour
Canary rollout toggled via runtime flag and observed metrics show <0.05% increase in 5xx or malformed-output errors during canary window
Documentation updated (runtime contracts + error codes) and PRD link added to ticket
Security review completed and approved for preserving customer-provided metadata and idempotency tokens
tasks: Design: finalize fallback scoring formula and mid-stream contract (Alyssa) — design doc linked
Runtime: implement name-mapper and scoring hooks in router (Diego) — runtime-commit branch
Streaming shim: implement fallback-event chunk and validate structured output schema preservation (Eng Streaming Team)
Telemetry: add events for alias_resolution_attempt, alias_resolution_result, fallback_triggered, fallback_completed
Tests: unit tests for mapper, integration tests against mock tools, chaos test for mid-stream tool failure
Rollout: create canary flag, prepare dashboard and alerts, run 24-hour canary on internal traffic
Docs: update API contract and ops runbook, add FAQ for customers
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Chose hybrid scoring: exact-match (priority), then lexical similarity (normalized names), then semantic embedding similarity (title+description) with tunable weights — balance favors precision to avoid incorrect fallbacks.

2025-02-17: Mid-stream fallback contract chosen: emit a 'fallback-event' stream chunk containing {original_alias, chosen_canonical, confidence, provenance_token} then either continue the chosen tool's stream if compatible or emit terminal degradation token 'FALLBACK_NO_STREAM' with structured error schema.
2025-02-20: Decision to preserve idempotency_token from caller in provenance metadata and encrypt it in logs for PII safety — requires security review.
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Setup prototype mapper service and toy dataset of 150 alias->canonical mappings from historical telemetry
2025-02-16: Implemented lexical normalizer (lowercase, punctuation strip, common stopword removal) and verified reduces alias variance by ~42% on sample corpus
2025-02-19: Added embedding-based candidate scorer using model-embed-1-small; initial thresholds tuned on 200 labeled pairs (precision 0.94 at recall 0.78)
2025-02-24: Streaming shim implemented and unit-tested locally; edge-case: partial JSON chunks with trailing commas handled via buffering strategy
2025-02-28: PRs opened for runtime and shim; telemetry schema proposed and awaiting review
qa_plan: Unit tests for mapper normalization, lexical and semantic scorers
Integration test harness that simulates tool backends returning streaming and non-streaming outputs; assert no malformed structured outputs
Chaos tests: kill primary tool mid-invocation and assert fallback stream contract observed
Performance test: measure latency impact on median P50 and P95 for router path with scoring enabled (target <2ms added latency on P50)
rollout_plan: Canary 1: 1% internal traffic for 4 hours, monitor errors and structured-output validation dashboard
Canary 2: 10% internal+beta customers for 24 hours, run smoke tests on customer-facing endpoints
Full rollout conditional on canary metrics and security sign-off
Backout plan: disable flag and unroute in-flight requests; run remediation job to reprocess any failed structured outputs if necessary
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: fallback_rate > 0.5% for 5m AND malformed_structured_output_rate increased by >0.02% -> P0 paging
Alert: canary_error_delta > baseline by 20% -> auto-disable flag and notify owners
Logs: store resolution decisions with hashed provenance_token and request_id for audit
notes: Design review scheduled 2025-02-15 with Runtime, Streaming, and Security teams — action: add encryption for provenance_token in logs
PM requested visible telemetry for customers to opt-in to alias suggestions in a future ticket
Edge case: plugins that use 'function-like' tools with side-effects need explicit allowlist; proposed allowlist managed by Dedicated/Private configs
